# Range oven: physical model, evidence, and validation

**Status: force-tested engineering model, not calibrated sim-to-real equivalence.** Exact product ID, component weights, hinge torque curve, latch force and tape scale were not supplied. Simulated numbers below are measurements of this model, not measurements of the real appliance. No force, spring, damping or mass value was measured from the video. This deliverable remains in the explicitly requested mechanism folder; it introduces no new capture and does not relocate the upstream scene to `test_scene_N`.

## Evidence and metric scale

Source: `../../assets/range_oven/range_body` (`model.blend`, `model.json`, `parts/*.obj`, `collision/*.obj`), plus the separate `oven_storage_drawer` and `oven_wire_rack` assets. Geometry and photographed materials are reused, not replaced by a generic range. `evidence/source_geometry.json` freezes their dimensions and world registrations. The upstream assets were revised concurrently during this task. The final package therefore includes an immutable `source_asset/` snapshot and `evidence/source_sha256.json`; build, visual extraction and rendering use this snapshot. `freeze_source.py` is the explicit refresh operation. The last validation uses only this frozen revision, including its 2 mm drawer floor and raised handle. `../../layout/structure.json`, `../../layout/parts.json` and `../../../gs_sim/articulation.json` are the upstream observations.

The reference frame is the original range body's bottom centre, metres, +Z up, +Y front. Root is installed/fixed. Frozen source world translation is [0.045, -1.063145, 0.015] m; it is removed from this standalone asset. The assembled drawer extends 3.2 mm beyond the body's right envelope owing to upstream registration uncertainty; the frame is the body's centre, not a recomputed movable assembly AABB.

| Quantity | Supplied reconstruction | Status / comparison |
|---|---:|---|
| Complete range body visual envelope W × D × H | 0.880 × 0.86071 × 1.216 m | Source visual bounds, including handle/backguard |
| Structural main shell W × D × H | 0.870 × 0.690 × 0.925 m | Supplied measured layout envelope |
| Door width × height | 0.841762 × 0.595838 m | Constrained multi-view fit; confidence 0.45 |
| Re-run raw f3397 door plane | 0.8442 × 0.5856 m | ktools; 0.401 inlier fraction; saved in evidence/door_remeasurement.json |
| Door hinge local position | [0.0177899972, 0.3618951142, 0.2669000030] m | Original constrained joint |
| Door axis | [-0.999121666, 0.016910028, -0.038340062] | Original axis, normalized; positive opens outward |
| Door angle range | 0–1.55 rad (88.81°) | Supplied near-90° stop; f3459=1.55, f3483=1.4257 rad |
| Drawer W × D × H | 0.846 × 0.5355 × 0.212 m | Measured front / hidden tray assumptions |
| Drawer body position | [0.020185, 0.116501, 0.020] m | Difference of source world origins |
| Drawer axis / travel | [0,1,0] / 0.400 m | Horizontal engineering rail assumption; opening not observed |
| Rack W × D × H | 0.670 × 0.504 × 0.01030003 m | Source rack geometry |
| Upper / lower rack origins | [0,-0.011855,0.636] / [0,-0.011855,0.459] m | Source registration |
| Rack axis / travel | [0,1,0] / 0.380 m each | Assumed pull-out stop, not measured |

The ktools command was run from the project root with `--root scenes/kitchen_1/gs_sim rect f3397 '210,741.565574 1258,659.613583 1144,1193.300937 324,1301.237705'`. It reproduced the upstream raw measurement. The constrained dimensions remain authoritative for assembly. Source f0772 gives a different door width (0.762847 m), which is additional evidence of uncertainty rather than a second precise dimension.

The photographed logo resembles Whirlpool, but the exact model is not established. Whirlpool's [W10252706 dimension guide](https://www.whirlpool.com/content/dam/global/documents/201001/dimension-guide-W10252706-D-WH.pdf), covering GFE461LV and related 30-inch electric ranges, lists width 0.759 m, depth including handle 0.699 m, overall height 1.191 m and cooktop height 0.914 m. These are comparison specifications, not identification of this appliance. The reconstructed width is 15.9% above that width, depth 23.1% above the comparison depth, but height only 2.1% above it. **A single uniform scale is not proven to resolve this discrepancy.** Do not silently force the assembly to 30 inches. Upstream metric scale is depth-derived (0.1632594913 m/reconstruction unit; roughly 4% reported depth error), not tape calibrated. No centimetre-accuracy claim is justified.

`params.py` is the parameter dictionary and loads the frozen source dimensions from `evidence/source_geometry.json`. `metric_scale` scales all source mesh vertices, offsets, primitive dimensions, latch gap and slide travel. Mass stays fixed; geometry-derived inertia scales with scale²; counterbalance stiffness scales inversely with scale; optional knob spring stiffness scales inversely with scale². Joint friction, damping, hinge angles and generalized spring coefficients stay fixed and must be revalidated after calibration. The 0.9-scale build check verifies mass invariance, inertia² scaling, prismatic travel scaling and unchanged hinge range (`tests/scale_results.json`). A global correction cannot address independent shape errors.

## Mass and inertia

The complete touch-control model is 76 kg: 57.392 kg fixed shell, 10 kg door including 0.8 kg handle/brackets, 6 kg empty drawer, two 1.3 kg racks, and one 0.008 kg button cap. The optional two knobs add 0.090 kg. Latch pads, rail capsules and spring sites are massless equivalent hardware; their mass is included in the shell/door budgets. No towel, hood, cookware, drawer contents or food is included by default. Payload tests use separate 0.25 kg objects.

76 kg is an unmeasured engineering prior retained from the upstream asset, with an explicit complete-appliance mass budget. As a real-product plausibility comparison, GE lists [JB258GMSA net weight 155 lb](https://www.geappliances.com/appliance/GE-30-Free-Standing-Self-Clean-Electric-Range-JB258GMSA), about 70.3 kg. It is a different product and does not determine this appliance's mass. Door 10 kg follows the requested 8–12 kg insulated glass-door prior and replaces the unsupported 13.68 kg fraction. Drawer 6 kg and each rack 1.3 kg retain the initial upstream unmeasured component priors (the later frozen asset revision instead guesses 4.1 kg / 1.55 kg; neither set is measured); 45 g plastic knobs and 8 g cap are small-hardware priors. None are sold as manufacturer component specifications.

Each explicit inertia is a volume integral of the component geometry, with its assigned mass, combined using the parallel-axis theorem. Door panel proxy receives 9.2 kg; the bar and two mount proxies share 0.8 kg in proportion to their volumes. Shell/drawer component masses are proportional to convex proxy volumes; this is a homogeneous composite approximation, not steel density applied to the exterior volume. Rack inertia uses the complete cylinder grid, scaled to 1.3 kg. Collision capsules have rounded tips while inertia cylinders have flat tips (sub-millimetre end-cap approximation). Button/knob primitive inertia is computed by MuJoCo from their mass and shape. All tensors are about each COM in its local body frame, not about the hinge. Full off-diagonal tensors and mass splits are in `evidence/inertias.json`; compiled principal inertias, including cap/knobs, are in `evidence/compiled_bodies.json`.

| Body | Mass kg | COM local m | Tensor diagonal kg·m² |
|---|---:|---|---|
| range_body | 57.392 | [-0.0, -0.1308463, 0.6277832] | [8.2102622, 10.616508, 8.1201246] |
| range_door | 10 | [-0.0117581, -0.0078945, 0.302829] | [0.2926911, 0.8105305, 0.5279764] |
| range_drawer | 6 | [0.0, 0.1927, 0.093498] | [0.1368842, 0.3872707, 0.4735823] |
| range_rack_0 | 1.3 | [0.0, 0.0004826, 0.0061391] | [0.0358556, 0.0600302, 0.0958683] |
| range_rack_1 | 1.3 | [0.0, 0.0004826, 0.0061391] | [0.0358556, 0.0600302, 0.0958683] |

## Passive mechanisms

There are no position servos, gravitycomp flags, force callbacks, hidden equality switches or motorized opening behavior in the MJCF. Reset to keyframe **`rest`**; all qpos/qvel are zero and both adhesion controls equal **1**. A plain MjData reset leaves ctrl=0 and disables the latch until explicitly set. `rest` is the one requested exception to the `range_` name prefix. All other named elements and defaults use that prefix.

| Joint class | Dry frictionloss | Viscous damping | Armature | Joint spring stiffness / reference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| range_door | 0.9 N·m | 2.5 N·m·s/rad | 0.015 kg·m² | 0.6 N·m/rad; 0.65 rad |
| range_drawer | 7 N | 18 N·s/m | 0.05 kg | 0; reference 0 m |
| range_rack | 4 N | 8 N·s/m | 0.02 kg | 0; reference 0 m |
| range_knob | 0.035 N·m | 0.004 N·m·s/rad | 0.00001 kg·m² | 0; reference 0 rad; additional periodic tendon below |
| range_button | 0.15 N | 1 N·s/m | 0.002 kg | 1500 N/m; reference 0 m |

These are explicit engineering assumptions. Door dry friction represents bushings/hinge cam drag and a small holding band; its damping dissipates roughly 2.5 N·m at 1 rad/s. Drawer 7 N represents roller/rail starting resistance; 18 N·s/m adds 3.6 N at a 0.2 m/s hand pull. Rack 4 N corresponds approximately to dry rail drag for a 1.3 kg rack (4/(1.3×9.81)=0.314 equivalent coefficient); 8 N·s/m adds 1.6 N at 0.2 m/s. Armatures are small equivalent hardware/roller inertia, not masses measured separately; they are additional generalized inertia. Damping and friction are not fitted to source-frame trajectories.

**Counterbalance.** Two passive spatial springs use zero equivalent rest length and each has stiffness 408.75 N/m at nominal scale. Their fixed anchors are 0.12 m vertically above the hinge, displaced ±0.30 m along the actual hinge axis; moving sites are displaced the same amount from the door COM. Because displacement along the hinge axis is invariant, their summed potential equals +mg·COM_z plus a constant. This cancels gravitational door torque throughout rotation without supplying net cycle energy. The small 0.6 N·m/rad joint spring gives a preferred position at 0.65 rad and is weaker than the 0.9 N·m static holding band throughout normal travel. This reproduces broadly balanced opening as requested. It is an **ideal equivalent of preloaded/cammed hinge springs**, not literal zero-free-length coils or measured hidden hardware. A real range may hold only specific detents and needs a measured torque-angle fit before this approximation is accepted. The displayed orange lines illustrate the equivalent force paths, not reconstructed spring placement.

**Closed latch.** Each of two dedicated welded child bodies owns only an 8 mm radius spherical gasket pad. A paired striker sphere touches it at q=0. Pad centres are 0.49 m above the hinge in the measured door plane, with ±0.30 m lateral offsets. Each `adhesion` actuator contributes a total **12 N**, ctrl=1. Explicit gasket/striker contact pairs use a **0.6 mm detection margin and gap**. The gap permits adhesion to persist over the tiny inactive contact band while ordinary compression begins at zero separation. Thus adhesion exists only while that designated pair has a MuJoCo contact; it is not an angle-only torque. Isolating pads on child bodies prevents adhesion from pulling on a robot gripper, rack or door panel. The resulting approximate breakaway torque is 24×0.49=11.76 N·m before hinge drag, divided by the actual measured handle lever arm (computed from the raised source handle, approximately 0.59 m). The 18–26 N acceptance band is an assumed moderate one-hand pull, not a published or measured force for this oven. Spheres are a stable equivalent striker/gasket patch, not a full compressible gasket simulation. There is no evidence that the real oven has magnets; adhesion is a latch surrogate, not a material claim. The self-cleaning safety lock is not modeled.

**Opening transient.** There is no invented spring ejector. The reported “pop” is motion after a defined external pull pulse breaks contact; momentum and weak hinge bias lead to a small settled opening. Merely separating the latch does not imply a measured real-world automatic pop angle.

**Drawer.** An open tray slides on an ideal 1-DOF guide with two compliant travel limits. It retains 6 kg when empty. The original inferred rail direction [0.0271,0.99734,0.06766] would rise ~27 mm over full travel and was inferred from the closed front, not an opening observation. It is replaced by horizontal +Y rails; this avoids turning plane-fit noise into a gravity-loaded slide. Rail rollers, lateral play, lift-out and nonlinear load-dependent rolling resistance are lumped into the joint, not rigidly meshed rollers.

**Racks.** Two independent slides run on side rails, with 29 convex capsule collision members each: four perimeter bars, 23 fine longitudinal wires and two transverse supports. The 0.38 m limit represents the retaining stop; removing/lifting the rack is excluded by the prismatic constraint. Rails are physical visible/contactable capsules and the ideal joint carries guide reactions. Food/cookware is separate; adding payload increases reaction forces but the chosen joint frictionloss does not automatically scale with payload. This is a limitation for heavily loaded racks.

**Controls.** f3397/f0772 and the upstream inventory show flush touch controls; they do not show rotary knobs. The main file preserves this configuration and adds one representative 8 g pressable cap at [0.16,-0.353,1.12] m, half-size [0.009,0.002,0.007] m. Its 0.8 mm inward -Y travel, 1500 N/m soft spring and stiff limit approximate a membrane switch. Actual switch travel/type is unobserved; it might instead be capacitive. No electrical behavior or power switching is claimed. The hypothetical `range_with_knobs.xml` adds two continuous revolute 45 g knobs, radius 22 mm and half-depth 12 mm, rotating about +Y. Each has an eccentric zero-rest-length tendon giving **-0.025 sin(q) N·m**, one stable OFF detent per full turn, plus 0.035 N·m friction. There is no angular limit or push-to-turn interlock. It is a reusable requested mechanism, not a claim about photographed hardware.

## Collision, materials and solver values

Visual meshes have contype/conaffinity=0; collision geometry remains enabled, including parent/child pairs (`filterparent=disable`). The shell uses 12 source convex pieces (two exterior sides, two liners, rear, floor, top, backguard and four feet) and four rail capsules. Door uses the original inset 0.78×0.040×0.53 m oriented panel and the source handle bar plus two mount colliders. Five drawer pieces preserve its hollow interior. The drawer front collider's upper edge is lowered by 1 mm to remove a 0.159 mm interference at the measured full-open door pose. This is a documented collision clearance change; decorative geometry is preserved. Interior volume is not replaced by a convex hull. Rack fine-wire collisions replace the previous eight coarse interior contact bars. Body meshes remain fixed; no anti-tip bracket or free-base motion is solved. The frozen revision includes backguard/foot collision proxies. Foot colliders are shortened from 35 mm to a 15 mm lower support region, giving 5 mm clearance below the drawer bottom at 20 mm; the original hidden 35 mm proxies penetrated the closed drawer. This is an assumed contact simplification of the leveling feet/stems; the visual feet are preserved.

All collision primitives are convex; imported collision OBJ meshes are closed convex boxes. Intra-body overlapping pieces do not self-collide. Contact tests cover both ordinary intended operation and pushing a rack against the door. The observed <2 mm bound is for these tested forces/speeds, not arbitrary impacts or every possible payload.

| Surface | Sliding coefficient | Torsional length m | Rolling length m | Justification |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Default sheet/enamel / floor | 0.35 | 0.003 | 0.0001 | Moderate dry steel/enamel prior; floor is support only |
| Handle and optional knob grip | 0.80 | 0.003 | 0.0001 | High grip-contact prior, not a measured steel coefficient |
| Gasket/striker | 0.70 | 0.002 | 0.0001 | Compliant high-friction gasket prior |
| Rack wire | 0.25 | 0.001 | 0.0001 | Smooth/discoloured steel contact prior |

MuJoCo's torsional and rolling coefficients have length units. condim=3 means the supplied torsion/rolling values are dormant unless a consumer enables 4/6-dimensional contact. Explicit latch pairs use [0.7,0.7,0.002,0.0001,0.0001] friction parameters and condim=3. Material appearance is inherited from source photographs (brushed steel, black glass, dark enamel, discoloured wire); roughness/metalness are artistic estimates, not measured reflectance. Original panel/floor single-sided OBJ triangle winding was corrected for MuJoCo visibility. Blender beauty renders retain the original material nodes; MuJoCo has a simpler material approximation: specular=0.4, shininess=1−source roughness, and reflectance=0.25×source metallic fraction. Towels are omitted rather than simulated as rigid hanging masses.

- Gravity [0,0,-9.81] m/s²; step 0.001 s; implicitfast integration; 100 solver iterations; tolerance 1e-10; energy computation enabled. These are numerical choices, not physical parameters.
- Ordinary contact `solref=[0.003,1]`, `solimp=[0.99,0.999,0.0005,0.5,2]`.
- Joint limits `solreflimit=[0.003,1]`, `solimplimit=[0.95,0.99,0.001,0.5,2]`; limits are compliant physical end stops, not clamped qpos.
- Gasket pairs and button travel stop use `solref=[0.002,1]`; gasket `solimp` matches ordinary contact. A short critically damped response reduced high-speed reclosure penetration.
- Friction constraints use `solreffriction=[0.004,1]`, `solimpfriction=[0.9999,0.99999,0.001,0.5,2]`. High impedance reduces creep under subthreshold loads. These solver settings are numerical surrogates for stiff hardware; widths for hinge constraints use radians and slide/contact widths use metres.

## Force experiments and results

`tests/test_physics.py` runs unittest without pytest. Forces are applied through `xfrc_applied` in world coordinates at handle/button sites: F on the body COM plus torque (site−COM)×F. Door/knob loads follow the instantaneous tangential direction; slider loads are +Y, button loads -Y. qpos is only set to initialize test poses; opening, travel, stop compression and return are produced by applied force and passive physics. Every dynamic step checks finite qpos/qvel/qacc, samples contact distance, and final checks reject MuJoCo warnings. Energy decay is checked only after external force removal and outside adhesive contact, so adhesion power is not confused with passive dissipation.

**12 MuJoCo tests: passed.** MuJoCo 3.5.0. Test-suite wall time 39.759 s (includes model loading and Python assertions; not reconstruction throughput). Per-experiment simulation and stepping wall times are retained in `tests/results.json`. Tests may overlap in recorded trace intervals; do not sum repeated checkpoints as unique simulation time.

| Measurement | Actual simulation result | Acceptance / protocol |
|---|---:|---|
| Door breakaway | 21.0 N | 18–26 N; >0.02 rad in 0.5 s; 0.5 N resolution |
| Pull-pulse settled angle | 8.994° | 25 N for 80 ms after 0.3 s settle; release 4 s; 0.03–0.25 rad |
| Open stop | 88.8090° | 40 N tangential pull for 3 s; limit 1.55 rad |
| Drawer travel | 400.0004 mm | 5 N holds; 9 N breaks away; 30 N reaches 400 mm stop |
| Rack travel | 380.0036 mm | 3 N holds; 6 N reaches 380 mm stop, both racks |
| Maximum tested penetration | 1.3206 mm | ≤2 mm in dynamic and payload tests |
| Initial / 101-pose door sweep penetration | -0.0000 mm | No initial overlap; sweep with other parts at rest |
| Door passive energy loss | 0.254535 J | After 12 N, 150 ms excitation; decays for 4 s |
| Half-step pulse-angle difference | 0.000846 rad | <0.015 rad at dt 0.001 vs 0.0005 s |

Additional assertions verify rest stability, 0.25/0.775/1.30 rad partial-open holding, automatic relatching after a closing force, adhesion zero generalized force away from contact, both directions of drawer/rack stops, stiff second-stage button travel and release, continuous knob rotation beyond 2π, damping settling, and 0.25 kg payload support on the open rack/in the open drawer. The unexpected rack/closed-door interaction is allowed to push the door open physically; it is not bypassed by disabling collision. `tests/package_results.json` also confirms both exported XML files load from an isolated copy containing only mjcf/, all imported collision meshes are convex/watertight with positive volume, and positive principal inertias satisfy the triangle inequality. `tests/traces.json` stores 100 Hz traces: time, all qpos, all qvel, potential and kinetic energy. Traces use 5 DOFs for the real configuration and 7 for the optional knob configuration; q order is door, drawer, upper rack, lower rack, button, then knobs. Main `results.json` is the canonical MuJoCo report.

The three separate Torch tests in `tests/isaac_kernel_results.json` check tilted-axis counterbalance against MuJoCo, contact/angle-gated latch torque, button stiffness and periodic knob torque. **Isaac Lab/PhysX runtime has not been tested because it is not installed.** `isaac/actuators.py` supplies a genuine ActuatorBase/ActuatorBaseCfg implementation for Isaac Lab 2.2.x when installed, and fails clearly if configuration is requested without it. Native PhysX friction is set to zero because a friction coefficient is not MuJoCo frictionloss in N/N·m; explicit smooth Coulomb torque/force uses tanh(v/0.0005), which permits small creep and is not exact stiction. Explicit damping equals the table, and armature is assigned in the config. The button's second stage uses an 80000 N/m penalty beyond 0.8 mm, with imported USD travel limits still required. Gasket contact masks must come from the two filtered pad/striker distance pairs every step; masks are cleared after use. Latch torque is capped to the first margin/arm ≈0.001224 rad and requires contact. Its 11.76 N·m combined nominal torque is an approximate moment surrogate for the actual contact-normal geometry. Import geometry, inertia and joint limits, enable self-collisions, fix the base, remove drives, wire the contact-distance sensor, and repeat the force suite in PhysX before claiming equivalence. Do not apply this actuator's gravity counterbalance on top of imported passive counterbalance tendons.

## Review, reproducibility and remaining calibration

`review.jpg` combines rest, half-open, full-open, actual MuJoCo collision/spring cutaway and recorded force/travel/energy plots. Beauty poses are offline Blender views of original materials at MJCF angles; they are not independent evidence of dynamics. `renders/force_travel.pdf` is the standalone plot artifact. Blender render wall time and version are in `renders/timing.json`. No synchronized capture/reconstruction was acquired here; upstream offline source-camera replay remains at `../../layout/replay/index.html` with `reconstruction_replay.mp4`. This mechanism work does not claim online estimation or publish a personal-site case study with unverified physical performance.

To calibrate the real appliance, obtain its model label, tape width/depth/door hinge-to-handle distance, detached component masses or manufacturer mass data, slow handle force versus door angle in both directions, latch breakaway over repeated pulls, drawer/rack starting/running forces (empty and loaded), and release trajectories. Those values distinguish spring torque from friction and damping. Refit parameters and re-run all force tests after the pending scale job; current acceptance bands are engineering targets. No undisclosed force fit or precise real-world match is claimed.

Material numerical values are preserved in `evidence/visual_manifest.json` (each material's RGBA, roughness, metallic fraction, and texture).
